title: What is Heteroskedasticity?
summary: This video explains the technical definition of heteroskedasticity, why it matters in regression analysis, how to detect it using residual plots and tests like Goldfeld-Quandt and Breusch-Pagan, and how to remedy it using robust standard errors.

concepts.name: Heteroskedasticity
concepts.summary: Heteroskedasticity occurs when the variance of the error term (or Y given X) is not constant across observations.

concepts.name: Homoskedasticity
concepts.summary: Homoskedasticity refers to a regression model having a constant, even spread of error terms across all values of X.

concepts.name: Goldfeld-Quandt test
concepts.summary: The Goldfeld-Quandt test evaluates the null hypothesis of homoscedasticity by comparing the ratio of mean squared errors from two separate regressions.

concepts.name: Breusch-Pagan test
concepts.summary: The Breusch-Pagan test is a statistical test used to detect heteroskedasticity by examining whether the squared residuals depend on explanatory variables.

concepts.name: Heteroskedasticity-robust standard error
concepts.summary: Heteroskedasticity-robust standard errors (such as White's standard errors) provide a remedy to make statistical inference reliable when heteroskedasticity is present.
